notes: Magento 2 storefront, plain HTTPS fetch, no blocking. Investigated the site's discount/markdown area thoroughly: main nav mega-menu and homepage embedded nav-map JSON, footer, and full sitemap.xml (2 parts, ~370k URLs). The only markdown section is /sale-room1/ (title 'Cox & Cox - Sale'; meta description 'Discover stylish homeware for less in our Sale Room, with items at up to 50% off'; 124 products; no h1 rendered). Its entire URL structure is percent-off tiers (sale-room1/20-off/, /25-off/, /30-off/ ... /75-off/) plus category-scoped sale rooms (furniture-sale, lighting-sale, mirrors-sale, outdoor-sale, rugs-sale, soft-furnishings-sale, storage-sale, indoor-living-sale) and a seasonal 'christmas-sale' sub-branch with its own /25-off/ and /35-off/ tiers - i.e. a live promotional discount campaign, not a permanent end-of-line/outlet stock listing. Searched the page and full sitemap for the words 'clearance', 'outlet', 'final sale', 'end of line', 'last chance', 'discontinued' (English, the target-term list) - zero matches anywhere on the site. This matches the brief's own explicit exclusion example verbatim: 'a percent-off campaign with no permanence signal.' No genuine Clearance/Outlet-taxonomy page exists on this site. Not flagged as ambiguous because there is no clearance/outlet/permanence language anywhere and the URL taxonomy is unambiguously percentage-discount-driven, not end-of-line stock.
